title: Hook
text: Fire electrons at a wall with two narrow slits. Common sense says you should see two stripes on the screen behind it.
nxt: But what physicists actually saw is one of the strangest results in science, and it all comes down to whether anyone is watching.

title: Waves of Matter
text: In nineteen sixty-one, the physicist Claus Jonsson sent electrons through slits and saw a pattern of many light and dark bands,
nxt: the signature of waves overlapping. Matter was behaving like a wave.

title: One at a Time
text: In nineteen eighty-nine, a team in Japan led by Akira Tonomura sent electrons through the apparatus one at a time.
nxt: Each electron landed as a single dot, like a particle. But as thousands of dots piled up, the striped pattern slowly appeared.

title: Both Slits?
text: In standard quantum theory, the electron is described by a wave of possibilities that spreads through both openings.
nxt: Many physicists put it loosely by saying the electron goes through both slits.

title: The Detector
text: Now add a detector at the slits to find out which path each electron takes.
nxt: The moment the experiment records that information, the striped pattern disappears, and two plain bands remain.

title: Not a Mind
text: Does this mean a human mind changes reality just by looking? That is the most popular misunderstanding in physics.
nxt: What matters is whether the path information gets recorded in the physical world.

title: No Special Role
text: Nobody has found an experiment showing that consciousness plays a special role.
nxt: The observer in real laboratories is a photon detector, a bit of gas, a speck of dust.
